Gaze tracking

Quick access

  • API Subsystems Reference
  • Main Concepts

What is Combined Haptic and Gaze Interaction?

Combined Haptic and Gaze Interaction turns someone’s visual attention into physical sensation on another person’s body, using Teslasuit for haptics and a motion/eye-tracking system for targeting.

Scenario (at a glance)
  • Person A wears a Teslasuit.
  • Person B wears eye-tracking glasses.
  • A mocap system streams Person A’s body markers; the eye tracker streams B’s gaze origin and direction.
  • When B looks at a region on A’s body, the suit plays a localized haptic on that region-so A can physically sense being looked at.

Why this matters

  • Makes attention tangible: Person A feels where and when gaze lands.
  • Useful for training and social interaction studies.
  • Simple event-driven pipeline: track → intersect → stimulate.

Technically, the system senses gaze direction and marker geometry, computes a ray-quad intersection, and actuates stimulation accordingly. It is event-triggered (open-loop): stimulation parameters are set by the operator and not adjusted by real-time feedback.

Technically, the system senses gaze direction and marker geometry, computes a ray-quad intersection, and actuates stimulation accordingly. It is event-triggered (open-loop): stimulation parameters are set by the operator and not adjusted by real-time feedback.

Project Overview

  • Motion/Gaze Tracking: Receive 3D markers and gaze vectors from QTM in real time.
  • Haptic Feedback / FES: Create and play electrical stimulation touches on mapped suit channels.
  • Event-Triggered Control: Play a predefined touch whenever the gaze intersects a designated area.

Motion Capture Example

# Extract markers and gaze from a QTM frame
header, markers = packet.get_3d_markers()
quad = [np.array([m.x, m.y, m.z]) for m in markers[7:11]]
_, vectors = packet.get_gaze_vectors()
for _, samples in vectors:
    for uv, pos in samples:
        origin = np.array([pos.x, pos.y, pos.z])
        direction = np.array([uv.x, uv.y, uv.z])
        direction /= np.linalg.norm(direction)

Explanation:
A target quad is formed from four markers (indices 7-10). The gaze origin and a normalized gaze direction are taken from QTM’s gazevector component for intersection testing.

Haptic Feedback / FES Example

# Create and play a touch on mapped channels
layout = api.mapper.get_haptic_electric_channel_layout(device.get_mapping())
bones = api.mapper.get_layout_bones(layout)
channels = api.mapper.get_bone_contents(bones[TsBone2dIndex.Chest.value])
params = device.haptic.create_touch_parameters(100, 40, 150)
playable = device.haptic.create_touch(params, channels, 250)
device.haptic.play_playable(playable)

Explanation:
Channels are derived from the suit mapping (example uses the chest region). Touch parameters are period (ms), amplitude, pulse width, and playable duration (ms).

Closed-loop Control Example

# Event-triggered actuation in the frame callback
hit = gaze_processor.on_packet(packet)  # True if gaze ray hits the quad
if hit:
    haptics.create_haptic_touch(period_ms=period, amplitude=amp, pulse_width=pw)
    haptics.play_touch()

Explanation:
On each frame, the app checks gaze-quad intersection. If true, it (re)creates a touch with current operator parameters and plays it. This is open-loop, event-driven control.

Key Components

  • Motion Capture Sensors:
    3D markers and gaze vectors streamed from QTM provide the geometric context and gaze ray.

  • Haptic Channels:
    Suit electrodes are addressed via the mapping to target body regions with electrical stimulation.

  • Control System:
    An event detector performs ray-quad intersection; positive hits trigger a haptic touch.

  • User Interface:
    Operator-tunable stimulation parameters (e.g., period, amplitude, pulse width); logging for timing and events.

How the Key Components Work Together

  1. Motion/Gaze Tracking:
    QTM streams frames containing 3D markers and gaze vectors. The app builds a quad from four markers and extracts the gaze origin and unit direction.

  2. Intersection Test:
    The gaze ray is intersected with the quad’s plane; if the hit point lies inside the quad, a “hit” is detected.

  3. Stimulation Trigger:
    On hit, a touch playable is created (or reused) with operator parameters and played on the selected channels.

  4. Operator Control:
    Parameters like period, amplitude, and pulse width can be adjusted without changing the detection pipeline.

Example Workflow

  1. Setup: Connect Teslasuit; ensure it’s recognized by the SDK. Start QTM real-time streaming with ['3d', 'gazevector'].
  2. Designate Area: Place four markers to define the quad; adjust indices as per your layout.
  3. Stream & Detect: For each frame, compute gaze origin/direction and run the ray-quad test.
  4. Stimulation: On a hit, play a touch with safe, preconfigured parameters.
  5. Logging & Tuning: Record hits and timestamps; tune parameters (period, amplitude, pulse width) as needed.
  6. Iterate: Refine quad placement, thresholds, and stimulation settings for your protocol.
Warning

⚠️ Safety: Before using electrical stimulation, make sure the haptic system is calibrated and working. Start with conservative stimulation settings: low amplitude and short duration.

Note: This use case combines precise motion/gaze tracking with programmable electrical stimulation for immersive interaction and research. It operates in an open-loop, event-triggered manner rather than adaptive feedback control.
